title: Structa diagram
description: One diagram for Structa to draw. Text is plain text in Latin letters, digits and common symbols, with no control characters; runs of spaces collapse to one, and text can't be only spaces. Ids must be unique across nodes and edges, a row's id within its card, and an area's among the areas; "from", "to" and "about" must name a node that isn't a note (lines connect cards only, never areas), and a node's "area" and an area's "parent" must name an area.

version.description: the format version; leave it out to mean the current one

title.description: a title drawn at the top-left

description.description: a sentence or two drawn under the title

theme.description: the colours to draw in; the --theme flag and render()'s theme option win over it

direction.description: which way the diagram flows: top to bottom or left to right; by default right for ER diagrams, down for the others

groupAreas.description: true draws a box round each area's cards, nested as the areas are; otherwise each card shows its area as a tag

legend.description: false leaves out the legend of statuses and areas at the bottom

areas.description: named groupings that cards can be in, such as the parts of a system; drawn in this order

items.description: A named grouping of cards. Areas nest through "parent", at most 4 levels deep and never in a loop, and each must hold a card, directly or in an area inside it. Areas have no colours.

id.description: a unique id among the areas, made of letters, digits and - _ . :

label.description: the area's name, shown on its cards' tags or at the top-left of its box

parent.description: the id of the area this one is inside; leave it out for an outermost area

nodes.description: the cards, in reading order; the order gently guides the layout

items.description: One class. An enum (stereotype "enum") lists values instead of properties and methods, and only an enum has values. Its rows' statuses must agree with its own: a row in a new or removed card can only have the card's status, and takes it when it has none; a row in an unchanged card can only be unchanged; and a card needs a status when any of its rows has one. A card has at most 100 rows, all its lists together.

id.description: a unique id made of letters, digits and - _ . :

description.description: a short sentence drawn under the name

area.description: the id of the area the class is in

status.description: what the change does to this card; leave it out for no status

stereotype.description: what kind of class this is, drawn as a «…» line above the name

abstract.description: true draws the name in italics, as stereotype "abstract" does, without the «abstract» line

properties.description: the class's properties, in order; leave it out for none. Not for an enum

text.description: the member as you'd write it, such as a name and type or a signature

id.description: an id unique within the card; without one the row is known as properties[N]

visibility.description: drawn before the text: + public, - private, # protected, ~ package

status.description: what the change does to this row; leave it out for no status

methods.description: the class's methods, in order, drawn under the properties; leave it out for none. Not for an enum

to.description: the id of the node the line ends at

items.description: One table. Its columns' names are unique within it. Its columns' statuses must agree with its own: a column in a new or removed table can only have the table's status, and takes it when it has none; a column in an unchanged table can only be unchanged; and a table needs a status when any of its columns has one. A table has at most 100 columns.

description.description: a short sentence drawn under the name

status.description: what the change does to this card; leave it out for no status

name.description: the column's name, unique within its table

type.description: the column's type, such as uuid or varchar(200)

pk.description: true marks the column as part of the primary key, drawn as PK

fk.description: true marks the column as a foreign key, drawn as FK

unique.description: true marks the column's values as unique, drawn as UQ

nullable.description: true lets the column be null, drawn as ? after its type

status.description: what the change does to this column; leave it out for no status

fromCardinality.description: how many rows of the from table go with one row of the to table, drawn as a crow's foot at the from end

toCardinality.description: how many rows of the to table go with one row of the from table, drawn as a crow's foot at the to end

enforced.description: false shows a relationship the database doesn't enforce with a foreign key, drawn dotted

items.description: One part of a system. Every kind but "class" is a component card with its kind's icon and word. A node of kind "class" is a class card instead, with a class's fields: an enum (stereotype "enum") lists values instead of properties and methods. Its rows' statuses must agree with its own: a row in a new or removed card can only have the card's status, and takes it when it has none; a row in an unchanged card can only be unchanged; and a card needs a status when any of its rows has one. A card has at most 100 rows, all its lists together.
